name: FP8 on RDNA3 blows the 600 s engine-ready timeout on first start even though weights load in seconds
symptom: vLLM serve of an FP8 checkpoint on a gfx1100 Radeon aborts during startup with an engine-ready timeout after waiting VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S (default 600 s); measured first init was 1474.26 s. The message blames 'slow weight loading' while the weights actually loaded in 16.33 s, and the GPU sits idle.
root_cause: The wheel ships zero tuned W8A8 block-FP8 configs for device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics (218 device-keyed configs total: 76 AMD Instinct, 142 NVIDIA). With no config hit, warmup JIT-compiles the Triton GEMM kernels shape by shape on the CPU: W8A8 tuning alone searches 5 shapes for ~23.5 min, and first inference triggers a further ~43 min of Triton JIT staging that /health does not reflect.
workaround: Set VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800 for the first cold start. Once ~/.triton/cache is warm, engine init drops to ~49 s and later starts take ~2 min; the cost is one-time per host until that cache is cleared. Optionally drop tuned configs under both RDNA3 device-name strings (AMD_Radeon_RX_7900_XTX and AMD_Radeon_Graphics) as the issue reporter did.
notes: FP8 does work on gfx1100 - the blocker is cold-start cost, not an architecture refusal, despite community trackers listing FP8 as 'does not run on RDNA3'. Note the same thread reports Triton on RDNA3 hanging indefinitely at num_stages=5 and with BLOCK_SIZE_M=128/BLOCK_SIZE_N=256/num_warps=8.
